title: Tableau Pricing in 2026 by Role, Cloud and Add-Ons
summary: Tableau pricing charges per user monthly based on their role. You can compare Creator, Explorer, and Viewer costs, plus budget for hidden expenses.
body_markdown:
## Uncover hidden Tableau costs and limits


Check each item on a quote, because **five of them change the total** without touching the per-user price.


- Data Management and Advanced Management're available only in bundled editions since September 2024
- Server hosting and the admin labour to run it
- A premium for a single-year term over a longer commitment
- Limits on extract refreshes
- Whether Pulse and the AI features're included in your edition


When viewers ask to edit, they move up a tier, and each request adds to the bill.


### Server hosting, add-ons and refresh limits


A few terms on that list are worth pinning down. An extract refresh is the scheduled update of the copy of your data that Tableau stores for a dashboard. Pulse is Tableau's feature that sends plain-language summaries and alerts about the metrics you track.


Data Management covers cataloguing and preparing data sources, and Advanced Management adds administration, security and scaling controls for larger deployments.


Pick Cloud and Tableau runs the machinery. Pick Server and you do, so you pay for hardware, patching, upgrades and the person who does them. That labour never appears on the quote, but it lands on your payroll.


To get Data Management or Advanced Management you pay for the whole bundle, because they're no longer sold on their own.


Ask for written confirmation of what Pulse and the AI features require. I couldn't verify which editions include them, and assuming they're included is how a surprise invoice starts.


If your team needs hourly numbers, it may be reading yesterday's, because extract refresh limits cap how often your dashboards pull new data. I have no confirmed API limits to quote, so ask for them in writing.


Getting Tableau's numbers in front of people is a smaller job than the licence, and[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can take it on: it runs scheduled workflows around Tableau's API that send alerts and exports to the apps those people already use.


The run is the meter, at 1 credit whether the flow has two steps or ten, so splitting an export into smaller checks costs nothing extra, and the Free plan's 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows keeps this add-on small next to the seats.


Ask also about support tiers and the renewal uplift, since a discount in year one can reverse at renewal.
